option_description: Represents the number of days since the currently active managed WAF rule set version was last updated or refreshed, indicating how current the detection signatures are.
security_impact: The Rego rule_update_and_patch_currency rule enforces rule_set_version_age_days <= 30 as a required condition for both satisfaction paths. Rule sets older than 30 days may lack signatures for recently disclosed vulnerabilities, allowing attackers using new exploit patterns to bypass detection. A high age value indicates that newly discovered attack techniques such as novel SQLi variants or zero-day CMS exploits are not covered by current rules.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the AWS WAF managed rule group version list to identify the active version release date and calculate age in days.
how_to_obtain.command: aws wafv2 list-available-managed-rule-group-versions --vendor-name AWS --name AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet --scope REGIONAL | jq '.Versions | sort_by(.LastUpdateTimestamp) | last | {Name: .Name, LastUpdated: .LastUpdateTimestamp}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON output with LastUpdateTimestamp; calculate (today - LastUpdateTimestamp) in days. Values <= 30 indicate current rule sets.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For ModSecurity with OWASP CRS, check the installed CRS version file or package metadata to determine the release date of the current rule set.
how_to_obtain.command: cat /etc/modsecurity/crs/crs-setup.conf | grep -i 'version\|release'; dpkg -l | grep -i 'modsecurity-crs' || rpm -qi modsecurity_crs | grep -E 'Version|Release|Install Date'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CRS version and installation date displayed; compare install/build date against today to calculate age in days.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the WAF management console, navigate to the managed rule group details to view the currently applied version and its release date.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > WAF & Shield > Managed rule groups > [Rule Group Name] > Version history tab
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version history shows the active version with a release date; days since that date represents rule_set_version_age_days.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check WAF change logs or AWS Config change history to identify when the last rule set update was applied to the Web ACL.
how_to_obtain.command: aws configservice get-resource-config-history --resource-type AWS::WAFv2::WebACL --resource-id <webacl-id> --limit 5 | jq '.configurationItems[] | {captureTime: .configurationItemCaptureTime, changeType: .configurationItemStatus}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration change events showing timestamps of rule group updates; the most recent update timestamp determines the age in days.

option_description: Controls whether alerting or notification mechanisms are configured to inform the security team when WAF rule set updates are available or have been successfully applied.
security_impact: The Rego rule_update_and_patch_currency rule includes a path where update_notification_configured == true alongside auto_update_enabled == true and rule_set_version_age_days <= 30. Without update notifications, administrators have no visibility into whether automatic updates are succeeding, whether updates have been paused, or when new rule versions require review and testing before deployment. This low-criticality attribute ensures operational awareness of the update lifecycle.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check AWS SNS topics and CloudWatch Events rules configured to notify on WAF rule group version updates or AWS Security Hub findings related to WAF rule set changes.
how_to_obtain.command: aws events list-rules --name-prefix 'WAF' | jq '.Rules[] | {Name: .Name, EventPattern: .EventPattern, State: .State}'; aws sns list-subscriptions | jq '.Subscriptions[] | select(.TopicArn | test("WAF\|waf\|security"; "i"))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: EventBridge rules with WAF-related event patterns in 'ENABLED' state, or SNS subscriptions confirming notification endpoints are active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In AWS Console, check AWS Health Dashboard and Personal Health Dashboard for configured event notifications for WAF managed rule group updates.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > AWS Health > Health Dashboard > Event log (filter by WAF); also check CloudWatch > Alarms for WAF rule update events
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active event subscriptions or alert rules targeting WAF rule group update events with notification actions configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the WAF operations team or review runbook documentation to confirm a notification process exists for rule set updates, whether automated (email, PagerDuty, Slack webhook) or manual (change ticket workflow).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Review incident response runbooks, change management ticketing system, and team communication channels for WAF update notification procedures.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented procedure or active automated notification showing the team is informed when rule set updates occur.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For self-managed ModSecurity/CRS deployments, check if the update script sends email or webhook notifications upon successful or failed rule updates.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'mail|curl|webhook|notify|alert|slack' /usr/local/bin/update-modsecurity-crs.sh /etc/cron.d/waf-update 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Script contains notification commands (e.g., mail -s 'WAF rules updated', curl to a webhook URL) confirming update notifications are sent.

option_description: Controls whether geographic IP-based filtering rules are active and enforced in the WAF configuration, blocking or flagging traffic from high-risk or geographically restricted regions.
security_impact: The Rego geo_ip_and_reputation_based_filtering rule requires geo_ip_filtering_enabled == true alongside ip_reputation_filtering_enabled, a blocking action mode, and current threat feed data (threat_feed_update_frequency_days <= 7). Geo-IP filtering provides preemptive prevention by dropping traffic from geographies with no legitimate business purpose, reducing the attack surface for volumetric attacks, credential stuffing, and scanning campaigns originating from high-risk regions. This is a low-criticality attribute that contributes to the geo-reputation countermeasure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List AWS WAF Web ACL rules to identify geo-match statements that are actively enforcing blocks rather than operating in count/monitor mode.
how_to_obtain.command: aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name <webacl-name> --scope REGIONAL --id <webacl-id> | jq '.WebACL.Rules[] | select(.Statement.GeoMatchStatement != null) | {Name: .Name, Action: .Action, CountryCodes: .Statement.GeoMatchStatement.CountryCodes}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: GeoMatchStatement rules with Action set to 'Block' (not 'Count') and a list of CountryCodes confirms geo-IP filtering is active in enforcement mode.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Navigate to the WAF Web ACL rules list and verify geo-match rules are present with a Block action. For Cloudflare, check Security > WAF > Tools > IP Access Rules or Firewall Rules with country-based conditions.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > WAF & Shield > Web ACLs > [ACL Name] > Rules tab > identify GeoMatch rules and confirm Action column shows 'Block'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more geo-match rules visible with 'Block' action and specific country code lists; rules not in 'Count' or 'Monitor' mode.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For ModSecurity or NGINX-based WAF deployments, inspect the configuration for GeoIP2 module directives and deny rules targeting specific country codes.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'geoip2|GeoIP|deny|allow|country' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/*.conf /etc/modsecurity/*.conf
how_to_obtain.expected_output: geoip2 database path configured with deny directives for specific country codes (e.g., if ($geoip2_data_country_code = 'XX') { return 403; }) confirms geo-IP blocking is active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use a VPN or proxy service to simulate traffic from a blocked geography and verify the WAF returns a 403 block response, confirming enforcement mode is active.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sk --proxy socks5://<tor-or-vpn-proxy>:<port> 'https://<waf-protected-host>/' -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP Status: %{http_code}\n'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP 403 response when connecting from a blocked geography confirms geo-IP filtering is active and enforcing blocks rather than passively counting.

option_description: Controls whether the WAF actively evaluates incoming traffic against IP reputation databases and threat intelligence feeds, blocking or flagging requests originating from known malicious IP ranges, botnet infrastructure, and Tor exit nodes before they reach application logic.
security_impact: In the Rego policy, the geo_ip_and_reputation_based_filtering rule requires input.ip_reputation_filtering_enabled == true as a mandatory condition alongside geo_ip filtering and enforcement mode checks. If this attribute is false (the default), the entire geo_ip_and_reputation_based_filtering countermeasure fails to activate, leaving the WAF unable to preemptively block traffic from known-bad sources regardless of other filtering settings. Since this feature defaults to disabled, deployments that have not explicitly enabled it remain silently unprotected against reputation-based threats.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query AWS WAF v2 web ACL rules to check for IP reputation managed rule groups (e.g., AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList) using the AWS CLI.
how_to_obtain.command: aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name <web-acl-name> --scope REGIONAL --id <web-acl-id> --query 'WebACL.Rules[?Statement.ManagedRuleGroupStatement.Name==`AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList`]' --output json
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A non-empty JSON array indicating the AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList rule group is present and its OverrideAction is set to 'None' (meaning rules are actively enforced, not counted).

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the AWS Management Console, navigate to WAF & Shield > Web ACLs, select the relevant ACL, open the Rules tab, and look for 'AWS-AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList' or a custom IP reputation rule group. Verify it is listed and not overridden to Count mode.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > WAF & Shield > Web ACLs > [Select ACL] > Rules tab > Inspect managed rule groups for IP reputation entries
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The IP reputation rule group is visible in the rules list with Override action set to 'Use rule actions' rather than 'Count'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the Cloudflare API (if using Cloudflare WAF) to list firewall rules and confirm IP reputation rulesets are deployed and active in the zone's WAF configuration.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -X GET 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/<zone_id>/firewall/rules?per_page=100' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <api_token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' | jq '.result[] | select(.description | test("reputation"; "i"))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more firewall rules referencing IP reputation filtering are returned with 'paused: false', indicating active enforcement.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review WAF access logs or security event logs for entries tagged with IP reputation rule IDs (e.g., AWS rule IDs prefixed with 'AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList'). Presence of such log entries confirms the feature is active and evaluating traffic.
how_to_obtain.command: aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name <waf-log-group> --filter-pattern '{ $.terminatingRuleId = "AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList*" }' --start-time $(date -d '24 hours ago' +%s000) --output json | jq '.events[0:5]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log events are returned with terminatingRuleId matching the IP reputation rule group, confirming active evaluation and enforcement.

typical_values: false (default state; common in newly provisioned WAF instances that have not been hardened)

option_description: Specifies the interval in days between automatic refreshes of the geo-IP and IP reputation threat intelligence feeds used by the WAF. A lower value means the WAF operates with more current threat data, while higher values indicate stale intelligence that may miss recently identified malicious IP ranges.
security_impact: The Rego policy enforces input.threat_feed_update_frequency_days <= 7 as a condition for the geo_ip_and_reputation_based_filtering countermeasure to pass. This means if feeds are updated less frequently than weekly, the countermeasure is not credited even if IP reputation filtering is enabled and blocking mode is configured. Stale threat feeds allow newly compromised infrastructure, freshly added Tor exit nodes, and recently observed botnet IPs to bypass reputation-based blocking, undermining the entire preemptive filtering capability.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS WAF with managed rule groups, navigate to the AWS Security Hub or WAF console to check the managed rule group version and last update timestamp, which reflects how recently AWS refreshed the underlying threat intelligence.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > WAF & Shield > Web ACLs > [Select ACL] > Rules > [Select managed rule group] > View version details and 'Last updated' timestamp
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A 'Last updated' timestamp within the past 7 days confirms feeds are refreshed within the acceptable threshold.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the WAF provider's API for the managed rule group version metadata to determine when the threat intelligence feed was last updated.

option_description: Defines the enforcement action taken by the WAF when a geo-IP or IP reputation rule is triggered. Determines whether matching traffic is actively dropped (block), presented with a challenge such as CAPTCHA (challenge), passively logged without interference (monitor or log_only), or entirely bypassed (disabled). This setting directly controls whether reputation-based filtering has a preventive effect or serves only an observational purpose.
security_impact: The Rego policy condition input.filtering_action_mode in ['block', 'challenge'] is required for the geo_ip_and_reputation_based_filtering countermeasure to be satisfied. The default value is 'monitor', meaning that out-of-the-box WAF deployments will observe and log reputation-based matches but will not prevent any malicious traffic from reaching the application. Only 'block' or 'challenge' modes satisfy the policy, ensuring that known-bad IPs are actively prevented rather than silently permitted through the WAF with a log entry as the sole response.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS WAF, retrieve the web ACL configuration and inspect the override actions and rule actions for IP reputation rule groups to determine whether they are set to Block, Count, or another mode.

how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output shows 'OverrideAction: {}' (empty, meaning rule actions are used as-is) and individual rules within the group showing Action.Block rather than Action.Count, confirming block enforcement mode.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For ModSecurity-based WAF deployments, inspect the rule configuration to determine whether IP reputation SecRules use the 'deny' action (block) or 'pass'/'log' actions (monitor). Check the SecDefaultAction directive for the applicable rule phase.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'SecDefaultAction|SecRuleEngine|reputation|BLOCK_MODE' /etc/modsecurity/modsecurity.conf /etc/modsecurity/rules/*.conf 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^#'

typical_values: monitor (default; most common in initial WAF deployments during tuning phases)
block (recommended for production hardened deployments meeting policy requirements)
challenge (common for high-traffic consumer-facing applications where blocking entire IP ranges risks false positives)
log_only (observed in compliance-driven monitoring environments where availability concerns override prevention)
disabled (found in legacy configurations where specific rule groups were temporarily disabled and never re-enabled)
